title: Why Market Gaps Will Ruin Your Risk Management
text: One of the issue is markets can gap. So let's say that you sell a short strangle and you're planning on managing your risk at two times the credit you received. And there's a gap. Problem is if there's a gap, then you don't actually realize that managed risk level. So what happens here is we have a planned budget based on our risk tolerance, but then we have to accept the fact that there can be gaps if we're trading some sort of naked strategy. And for that you can think of managing it a few different ways. I would size that position either a little bit more conservatively if the thing I'm trading gaps a lot. And then the other thing beyond all of those is if you can hedge it. So for example, let's say I'm trading a short strangle in SPX. I can't trade SPX after hours. It's closed. What I can do is hedge with E-minis. For example, if the you know futures market is trading.
